steps.body: **Percent** is a rate with a fixed denominator: **per hundred**. "25 percent" means 25 out of every 100 — the ratio 25 : 100. Shade 25 squares of a hundred-grid and you can see it: 25/100, which shrinks to **1/4**. Percents are just ratios that always agree to run per 100, so any two can be compared at a glance.
Percent means per hundred — on a bar.

widget.successFeedback: 70 students. 35% means 35 per hundred, and there are two hundreds here — so 35 twice over. The bar makes the 'per hundred' visible instead of a rule to recall.
widget.lowFeedback: Less than 35% of the bar is shaded.
widget.highFeedback: More than 35% of the bar is shaded.

predict.prompt: Shading 35% of 200 students — will the shading reach past the halfway mark of the bar?
predict.reveal: Half the bar is 50 out of every hundred — 35 per hundred falls short of that mark, so the shading stops before the middle.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents percent meaning.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for percent meaning must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines percent meaning.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: One row of the hundred-grid is one tenth.

widget.prompt: What fraction, in simplest form, equals 10%?

options.feedback: That's 1%, a single square. 10% is ten squares: 10/100 = 1/10.
Equivalent, but not simplest — 10/100 reduces to 1/10.

steps.body: The bridge runs **both ways**. A fraction with denominator 100 is already a percent: 75/100 = **75%**. And friendly fractions convert by scaling to 100: 3/4 = 75/100 = 75%, because ×25 turns the 4 into 100. Learn the family — 1/2 = 50%, 1/4 = 25%, 3/4 = 75%, 1/10 = 10% — and most percent work is instant.

explanationVariants: 3/4 is three of four quarters, and each quarter is 25%.

widget.prompt: Write 3/4 as a percent. (Enter just the number.)

commonErrors.feedback: 34 mashes the 3 and 4 together. Scale the fraction to 100ths: 3/4 = 75/100 = 75%.
3 is just the numerator. Convert to per-hundred: 3/4 × 25/25 = 75/100 = 75%.

widget.prompt: Each card shows a value. Sort by which is equal to one half.

items.feedback: 5% is 5/100 = 1/20, far less than a half. Watch the decimal point in the percent.

widget.missFeedback: Put every card over 100 (or shrink to simplest form) and compare to 1/2 = 50/100. Only exact halves belong left.
widget.successFeedback: Sorted — one half wears many outfits: 50%, 50/100, 0.5.

explanationVariants: A quarter of the hundred-grid is 25 cells shaded.

widget.prompt: On a 100-square grid, 1/4 of the squares are shaded. What percent is shaded?

commonErrors.feedback: 4 is the DENOMINATOR, not the percent. A quarter of 100 squares is 100 ÷ 4 = 25 squares = 25%.
14 mixes the 1 and 4. One quarter of 100 is 25: that's 25%.

hints: How many squares is a quarter of 100?
Put all three in the same form.
explanationVariants: As percents: 1/2 = 50%, 45% = 45%, 2/5 = 40% — so 2/5 is smallest and 1/2 is largest.
Convert everything to per-hundred and the order falls out: 40 < 45 < 50.

options.feedback: Close, but 2/5 = 40% is SMALLER than 45%. The order is 2/5, 45%, 1/2.

takeaways: Convert a fraction by scaling to 100ths: 3/4 = 75/100 = 75%.
The friendly family (1/2, 1/4, 3/4, 1/10) makes most percents instant.
steps.teaser: next: taking a percent OF a number.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Percent lives over 100.** To turn a percent into a fraction, write it over 100 and shrink: 20% = 20/100 = 1/5. To turn a friendly fraction into a percent, scale it to 100ths: 1/5 = 20/100 = 20%.

explanationVariants: Two rows of the hundred-grid is one fifth.

widget.prompt: What fraction, in simplest form, equals 20%?

options.feedback: That's 5%, one square in twenty. 20% is 20/100 = 1/5.
